title: POC scoping — workload signature & benchmarks (StrataWare)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to validate latency and cost targets for StrataWare's customer support assistant. Main goals: characterize QPS and concurrency patterns, define input/output token distributions, design benchmark harness, and agree success criteria and timeline.
topics: session affinity and cache hit rates
synthetic vs replayed prompts for benchmarks
action_items: Marcus Chen: share production request logs (last 30 days) or sanitized sample by 2026-11-09
Priya Nair: provide benchmark harness repo and runbook by 2026-11-06
Diego Ruiz: confirm VPC peering window and firewall rules by 2026-11-10
Jordan Lee: send draft POC statement of work and pricing estimate by 2026-11-05
next_steps: Redwood to ingest sample logs and return a traffic signature with recommended QPS and concurrency targets
Schedule a 1-hour benchmark design deep-dive w/ infra on 2026-11-09
Agree on POC start window (target week of 2026-11-16)
transcript:
Header:
Date: Wed Nov 4 2026 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (StrataWare CTO), Aisha Patel (Head of ML), Diego Ruiz (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Jordan: quick kickoff to scope the POC, we'll walk through your workload shape and agree success metrics, ok?
Marcus: sounds good, thanks.

--- Topics / Agenda ---
- high level goals and success criteria
- traffic shape (qps, spikes, concurrency)
- token distribution (input/output) and context window
- benchmarks: synthetic vs replay, metrics to capture
- timeline, infra and security checklist

[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off, this is a scoping for the POC for the cust sup assistant, primary outcome is we want to validate cost and latency targets, and also the integration story into your VPC for private data.
[00:22] Marcus: yup, priority is latency under load; our goal is p95 < 300ms on short responses and p99 < 800ms, but we'll see, those are aspirational.
[00:35] Priya: great, can you describe current traffic today, like qps and concurrency and any big daily peaks?
[00:47] Aisha: sure, average qps across all endpoints is about 12, peak during day hitting 130 qps for a 10-15 minute window, concurrency tends to be bursty because chat sessions fan out, typical session length is 3-5 turns.
[01:05] Diego: we also have long-running context sessions for higher-tier customers, those can hold context up to 8k tokens but only 2% of requests are that long.
[01:22] Jordan: that's helpful — so we need to model a heavy tail of token length. for benching we need both short prompts (~50 tokens) and long prompts (~4-8k).
[01:36] Marcus: correct, short questions like "how to reset password" are 20-60 input tokens and output 30-80; diagnostic workflows produce 2-4k outputs in worst case.
[01:52] Priya: do you have sample logs we can use or do you want us to synthesize?
[01:57] Marcus: we can share sanitized logs, but we need NDAs in place for full datasets, we can export a 30-day sample with IPs removed.
[02:10] Jordan: we'll take sanitized logs and also create a replay harness; replay is best for realistic latency distribution but synthetic helps isolate variables.

[02:30] Jordan: let's walk through success criteria — what would you call a successful POC?
[02:36] Marcus: three things — 1) confirm we can hit p95 latency targets under our production-shaped load, 2) reason about cost per 1M tokens and projection to scale, and 3) validate VPC connectivity + audit logs and RBAC for compliance.
[02:52] Aisha: and we want to test fallback behavior — what happens when capacity saturates, can Redwood route to a lower-cost model without changing api code.
[03:05] Priya: Redwood supports model variants and fallbacks; during the POC we can exercise canary and fallback policies. we should capture quality regressions though, so please pin a few eval prompts.

[03:25] Diego: on infra, two questions — do you support prefix/KV caching with session affinity? our platform relies heavily on KV cache to keep costs down.
[03:35] Priya: yes, the runtime supports KV caching, we call it KV cache but sometimes the transcript will say KV cash, so just to be clear it's the key-value attention cache. caching hit rate is critical — if you can show a 40% hit rate you will reduce token compute significantly.
[03:52] Marcus: what's a realistic hit rate for a chat application?
[03:55] Priya: for multi-turn support assistants we've seen 25-50% depending on session stickiness and whether you're reusing prefixes. if sessions are short and users ask similar clarifying questions, hit rate goes up.

[04:12] Jordan: let's quantify the traffic signature. from what you said, baseline: avg qps 12, daily peak 130, top-10 minute spikes to 160, concurrency typical ~40 with bursts to 450. does that match?
[04:28] Marcus: the burst to 450 is plausible if we include scheduled notifications, but that's rare — maybe once a week.
[04:36] Priya: we'll model both steady-state and 99th percentile bursts. for capacity planning we need to know token mix: percent of requests under 256 tokens in/out, percent between 256-1024, and percent above.
[04:51] Aisha: rough split is 72% under 256, 26% between 256-1024, 2% above 1024. output tokens skew heavier: many short inputs produce medium outputs 128-512.

[05:10] Diego: any constraints on model families? we have a preference for open models due to licensing but also want to compare quality/cost tradeoffs.
[05:18] Jordan: POC can include 3 variants — a small open model for latency baseline, a mid-size quantized model for cost/quality balance, and a larger model for quality validation. we'll provide recommended quantization profiles too.

[05:35] Priya: benchmark design — propose two phases: Phase A smoke: replay ~1 hour of traffic at 1x real-time to validate connectivity and metrics collection. Phase B stress: run accelerated replay with synthetic amplification to create peak bursts for 30-60 minutes to exercise autoscaling and fallbacks.
[05:57] Marcus: how do you accelerate safely so you don't break rate-limits and skew time-dependent behaviors?
[06:05] Priya: we scale time and preserve inter-arrival distribution where possible; for time-sensitive features we can keep sequences but amplify parallel sessions. we'll share the harness and you can review.

[06:20] Jordan: metrics we'll capture: cpu/gpu utilization, per-token cost, request-level latency (p50/p95/p99), tail latency for cold start, cache hit rate, model throughput, and model quality metrics on pinned eval set.
[06:36] Marcus: and we'll need logs routed to our SIEM — can you push structured logs and the audit trail?
[06:42] Jordan: yes, redwood supports export to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export, and we have audit logs with request-level metadata, though some fields can be redacted for PII.

[07:00] Aisha: for quality checks, we will provide an eval set of about 200 prompts and expected outputs; if you can show minimal degradation when falling back to smaller models that's a big win.
[07:12] Priya: agreed; we will compute BLEU/ROUGE and also human-inspected pass/fail for a subset. will the eval set include multi-turn contexts?
[07:21] Aisha: yes about 30% multi-turn sequences of 3-5 messages.

[07:35] Diego: security questions — we are enterprise and need SSO, RBAC, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence. what's your approach?
[07:45] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, and we can produce SOC2 docs and pen-test summaries under NDA. for the POC we can do a dedicated VPC peering and restrict egress.
[07:58] Marcus: okay, we'll queue the security checklist after this call.

[08:05] Priya: back to sizing, can you confirm the maximum context window you need? you said up to 8k tokens for a small percent — any more?
[08:12] Aisha: 8k is the upper bound for now, we have a few archival features that might need 16k in the future but not in this POC.

[08:21] Jordan: we'll include both 8k and a 16k-compatible path in recommendations but focus tests on 8k. note that larger context windows increase memory and affect batch sizing; we'll measure end-to-end throughput impact.

[08:38] Marcus: let's talk SLOs and guardrails — you mentioned fallback routing, what observable will trigger fallback?
[08:44] Priya: typically we set a latency budget per route; if p95 exceeds threshold for N minutes or queued requests exceed X, the router will divert to a compatible lower-cost variant. we'll also simulate a capacity outage during stress tests to ensure graceful degradation.

[09:02] Diego: on the topic of cost modeling, can you provide per-token compute cost estimates for the candidate model variants?
[09:07] Jordan: yes, we'll provide per-token cost, and then projected monthly cost for your traffic signature. we'll include sensitivity analysis for different cache hit rates and batching strategies.

[09:20] Aisha: batching — do you recommend large batch sizes for throughput? our latency SLO is strict so batch size is trade-off.
[09:27] Priya: we recommend dynamic batching with latency caps; continuous batching improves throughput but we cap batch wait at 10ms for strict latency routes, you can tune based on p95 observations.

[09:40] Marcus: what about startup/cold latency for new models or after autoscaling? we care about tail latency.
[09:46] Priya: cold start depends on model size and GPU pool configuration; we can keep warm pools and quantify cold start in stress tests. for p99 tail we instrument cold vs warm and report separately.

[10:00] Jordan: logistics — timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) finalize SOW and share logs, week 1 (ingest and traffic signature), week 2 (bench harness setup + smoke), week 3 (stress tests + metrics collection), week 4 (analysis + cost model + final report). total about 4-6 weeks depending on resource scheduling.
[10:22] Marcus: that aligns. we have a compliance window mid-nov so fastest start is week of 11/16.

[10:35] Priya: test data — for replay we'll need a mapping of user ids to anonymized ids to preserve session affinity; if you can't provide that we'll try synthetic session ids and note hit-rate differences.
[10:50] Diego: we can provide anon ids; full logs by 11/09.

[11:00] Jordan: ok next i want to capture the measurement plan specifics — what dashboards and reports do you want?
[11:05] Marcus: per-route latency breakdown, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit heatmap, and failure/error inventory. also a summary slide with recommended model variant for prod.

[11:20] Priya: during the POC we'll instrument per-token accounting and provide raw metrics plus dashboard links, and a spreadsheet with cost projection.

[11:30] Aisha: about model quality, if fallback reduces quality beyond thresholds we should abort fallback, so we need pass/fail rules.
[11:38] Jordan: define thresholds and we'll enforce them in routing policies during the test. e.g., if human-judged pass falls below 85% we won't use fallback for that route.

[11:50] Diego: any constraints on network egress? our infra team wants to limit IP ranges.
[11:55] Jordan: we can provide a small set of egress IPs and also use private peering; we'll work with your infra team.

[12:05] Marcus: are there any gotchas we should be aware of?
[12:09] Priya: watch out for tokenization differences across model families — token counts can vary and that affects cost. also for replayed traffic you may need to mask long-running websockets into discrete request/response pairs.
[12:22] Jordan: good point, we'll include tokenization normalization step in the pipeline.

[12:30] Marcus: ok to recap and next steps?
[12:33] Jordan: recap — Redwood to receive sanitized logs, Redwood to return traffic signature and recommended QPS/concurrency and model recommendations by 11/09, we'll schedule benchmark deep-dive on 11/09, target POC start week 11/16.
[12:47] Marcus: action items noted, thanks everyone.

--- End of call ---

Notes: transcript contains some ASR artifacts (names/acronyms slightly off e.g., "KV cash"), speaker turns occasionally merged.
